front_question: Define Tenths, Hundredths, and Thousandths as decimal place values.
How are currency (Paise to Rupees) and length (mm to cm to m) converted using decimal notation?
back_answer: Currency: 1 Paise = ₹0.01 (e.g., 45 p = ₹0.45). Length: 1 mm = 0.1 cm (e.g., 3 mm = 0.3 cm); 1 mm = 0.001 m.

front_question: Why are 0.2, 0.20, and 0.200 considered equivalent decimals, and how are they used in vertical addition?
back_answer: Appending trailing zeros to decimal places does not alter value (2/10 = 20/100 = 200/1000). Trailing zeros are added to align decimal places vertically before addition or subtraction.

front_question: Why is 0.2 greater than 0.09 despite 9 being greater than 2?
back_answer: Comparing digit place values from left to right: 0.2 has 2 in the tenths place (2/10), whereas 0.09 has 0 in the tenths place (0/10). Since 2 tenths > 0 tenths, 0.2 > 0.09.
